conceptZh: 披風英雄的長披風自己把他往後拉，倒著飛回「昨天」，筆畫也倒著落下。
object: a caped action-figure hero with a far-too-long cape
morph: the willful cape yanks the hero backward and the strokes of 昨 fall in rewind order
creativeAngle: 道具反抗：披風決定往回走，剛好對上「昨」的倒退意思。
promptEn: An 8-second animated clip on a pale lavender background, with one single Traditional Chinese glyph 昨 as the only text on screen, drawn in rich plum solid strokes, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with generous margins. 0-1.7s: a stout caped action figure strikes a hero pose and launches forward, but his crimson cape flops over his own head and he face-plants softly into a pillow cloud; the first 昨 is spoken as the right-hand 乍 strokes drop in from above. 1.7-3.4s: the cape grabs a lamp post and hauls him backward in a comic reverse-flight, legs pedaling; second 昨 as the left 日 slides in from the left like a rewinding film. 3.4-5s: 昨天 is spoken as the hero outsmarts the cape by tying it into a knot and a flutter of calendar pages (shapes only, no digits) blows backward behind him. 5-8s: hold; the hero stands, cape tidily knotted, giving a thumbs-up away from the glyph. Audio: a warm off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "昨、昨、昨天" (ㄗㄨㄛˊ、ㄗㄨㄛˊ、ㄗㄨㄛˊ ㄊㄧㄢ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between the two single utterances, and stops after the word; no other speech, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. Final 3 seconds (5-8s): the glyph 昨 is perfectly still and fully readable while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. Bright but not neon palette, no watermark, no flashing, no other writing.

conceptZh: 發條鯊魚看見橡膠恐龍用鼻子頂著一顆玩具太陽球就狂衝過去想咬，結果一頭撞上恐龍的大腳，撞得恐龍背上那疊日曆紙嘩啦散落排成右邊的「乍」，太陽球彈過來正好落成左邊的「日」，鯊魚暈著在旁邊轉圈，恐龍用整個身體把昨天那一頁往後翻。
object: a chunky wind-up toy shark, a rubber dinosaur balancing a bright toy sun ball on its nose with a stack of tall stiff calendar pages strapped to its back
morph: the crash jolts the calendar pages off the dinosaur's back so they fall and lock into the five strokes of 乍 on the right, while the sun ball bounces once and settles as the solid 日 on the left
creativeAngle: 前一版是披風英雄倒著飛的安靜轉場，這次改成可一眼看懂的衝刺撞擊：鯊魚想咬的太陽球就是「日」，撞散的日曆紙就是「乍」，撞擊本身直接堆出字形；「昨天」用恐龍整個身體把日曆頁往後翻、月亮探頭來具體表現，不靠文字。
promptEn:
An 8-second 2D cartoon clip on a soft butter-yellow background. The only text ever on screen is one Traditional Chinese glyph 昨, built from thick deep-teal solid strokes, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with clear margins. No other writing, no subtitles, no watermark, no flashing.

0-1.5s: Far left, a chunky wind-up toy shark with a big metal key turning on its back and a huge goofy toothy grin. Far right, a squat rubber dinosaur with enormous feet and comically tiny arms balances a bright orange toy sun ball on the tip of its nose, a tall stack of stiff cream calendar pages strapped to its back. The shark's eyes lock on the sun ball, pupils turning into little sun shapes; it chomps the air twice. The voice says the first 昨 as the shark digs its tail fin into the ground and leans way back, key whirring faster.

1.5-3s: The shark charges straight across the frame in a blur. The dinosaur tries to shield the ball but its tiny arms cannot reach, so it just turns its whole body sideways. The shark misses the ball and chomps a passing dust puff, spins once on dry land, resets even further back, and winds up bigger, cheeks puffed.

3-4.7s: Second charge at double speed. Freeze one beat an inch from the target. Then BONK: the shark squashes flat against the dinosaur's giant foot. The jolt shakes the calendar pages off the dinosaur's back; they tumble through the air and drop neatly into place on the right half as the strokes of 乍 (short left-falling stroke, vertical, top horizontal, then the two shorter horizontals and the hanging vertical), while the sun ball pops straight up, bounces once, and settles on the left half as the solid 日 box with its center bar. The second 昨 is spoken exactly as the last stroke clicks in and 昨 stands complete.

4.7-8s: The glyph 昨 holds perfectly still and fully readable in the center. Off to the right, the dinosaur, unable to use its arms, bows its whole body and flips one leftover calendar page backward with its chin as the voice says 昨天, and a tiny sleepy crescent moon peeks up from behind the page. The flattened shark peels itself upright, wobbles in a dizzy circle on the left margin with a dazed happy grin, then gives one proud little chomp at nothing, never touching the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly 昨、昨、昨天 (ㄗㄨㄛˊ、ㄗㄨㄛˊ、ㄗㄨㄛˊ ㄊㄧㄢ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between the two single utterances, and stops after the word. No other speech, no English, no written vocabulary. Soft cartoon boing and gentle bonk effects, light background music quieter than the voice. Bright but not neon palette, no pure white blowout, no dark grading.
